info.title: Workhorse dashboard API
info.summary: The RPC procedures behind the embedded Workhorse dashboard, contract dashboard/v1.
info.description: This API is served by your own Workhorse deployment at {origin}{basePath}, never by workhorse.run, which publishes only this document. Workhorse's primary protocol is SQL (ADR 0023): applications enqueue and work tasks through PostgreSQL, and these procedures are the operator surface the dashboard consumes, not an ingress API for application traffic. Every procedure is one POST with a JSON envelope. The HTTP path does not carry the contract version: each SDK release binds its backend to the matching dashboard contract and browser bundle (ADR 0054). A breaking change creates dashboard/v2, and its SDK release notes give operators the upgrade and deprecation notice. Deprecation and Sunset response headers do not apply because an installed backend serves one bound contract rather than negotiating concurrent versions. Reads go through the versioned dashboard_*_v1 SQL views and mutations through the shared versioned SQL functions, so any backend bound by this contract answers the same shapes. The document is generated from the committed dashboard/v1 artifacts (manifest.json, procedures.json, conformance.json) by pnpm dashboard-spec:generate and checked by pnpm dashboard-spec:check, so it cannot drift from the router.

servers.description: The deployment that embeds the dashboard.

origin.description: The scheme and host of the application serving the dashboard.

basePath.description: The dashboard mount path: /workhorse by default, an empty string when the dashboard owns the host root, or {path}/{workspace} when the host serves named workspaces.

tags.name: reads
tags.description: Procedures that read the versioned dashboard views. They accept any Origin and are served by read-only deployments.

tags.name: mutations
tags.description: Procedures that change state through the shared versioned SQL functions. They require a same-origin request, a writable deployment, and a host that wires the matching controller; each carries an audit block whose actor the server replaces with the authenticated principal.

dashboardSession.name: __Host-workhorse-dashboard-session
dashboardSession.description: Authorization is delegated to the host application, which may accept any credential it recognizes. A deployment without a host authorizer runs the built-in single-admin session instead: POST {basePath}/login with a form body of username and password sets this cookie, and POST {basePath}/logout clears it. An unauthenticated request answers 401 and an unauthorized one 403, both with a HostError body.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The body of every failed procedure call, under the same json key as a success. code is one of BAD_REQUEST, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; status repeats the HTTP status. Errors the host answers before a procedure runs use HostError instead.

HostError.description: The body the host answers before a procedure runs: authorization, workspace resolution, schema compatibility, and the same-origin check.

ValidationIssue.description: One input validation failure, as the request schema reports it. Keys beyond these three depend on the failed rule.

BadRequest.description: The envelope is malformed or the input failed the request schema. data.issues lists the failures when the schema produced them.

Unauthorized.description: No authenticated principal: the host's authorization rejected the request, or no single-admin session cookie was presented.

Forbidden.description: The host's authorization refused the authenticated principal.

MutationForbidden.description: Three refusals share this status. HostError bodies: the host's authorization refused the principal, or the same-origin check failed. Mutation procedures require an Origin header matching the request origin; a mismatched or unparsable Origin is rejected with status 403 before the procedure runs.
